solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Score as a writer

definitions.meaning: to score is to mark or scratch a line
a copyist or clerk who writes out documents by hand

explanation.surface: Someone takes up composing music as a career in letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to the same word: one marks lines with a pointed tool, the other is a professional copyist.

clue.text: Splendid organ effect

definitions.meaning: excellent, a dated colloquial word of approval
the crescendo produced by an organ's pedal-controlled shutter box

explanation.definitionFit: One word is old slang for excellent and also the organ's crescendo device and the sound it makes.

clue.text: Put out in unusual transport

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for unusual

parts.note: something unusual is rare

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word put are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone is turned out of an odd vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as annoyed or evicted, but 'out' alone is the anagram signal. Transport here is the emotional sense, being carried away with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport in the sense of being carried away by delight is a synonym for ecstasy.

clue.text: Spoiling the opening of Blackpool's Illuminations

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from the seaside town's name

parts.note: illuminations are lighting displays

explanation.surface: Something ruins the start of the famous light show at Blackpool.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blackpool Illuminations are an annual autumn light display along the seafront of Blackpool, an English seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A blight ruins crops, so blighting means ruining or spoiling something.

clue.text: It's said to have proved a hit

definitions.text: It's said to have proved a hit

parts.words: It's said to have proved a hit
parts.note: a fencer calls this French word to acknowledge being struck, and people use it to concede a telling point in argument

explanation.surface: A remark is reported to have been a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' suggests a popular success, but it is a fencing hit, acknowledged aloud by the one struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencer's cry admitting a touch is literally an acknowledgement that a hit landed.

clue.text: Has to renew promises

indicators.note: to renew is to make again, so these letters are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to make fresh vows.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn sworn promises are vows of this kind.

clue.text: Smoked chestnuts and hazel nut

definitions.note: a past participle standing for a noun: the thing that is smoked, a pipe made from a maize cob

parts.note: old chestnuts are stale jokes, and corn is trite, hackneyed humour
a cob or cobnut is a large hazelnut

explanation.surface: Roasted chestnuts and hazelnuts sound like a seasonal snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoked' looks like a cooking method for the nuts; it stands for a thing smoked, the pipe made from a maize cob.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe with a bowl carved from a dried maize cob is something one smokes.

clue.text: Choose exam for this sort of college

parts.note: to choose by voting is to elect
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A student is told to pick a test to get into a particular college.
explanation.walkthrough: The US body that formally chooses the president is the Electoral College, not a place of study.
explanation.definitionFit: The American body of presidential electors is called the Electoral College.

clue.text: A spider possibly saved Bruce from it

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given could form something else in another order

explanation.surface: Legend says Robert the Bruce took heart from watching a spider.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert the Bruce, the Scottish king, is said to have watched a spider keep trying to spin its web and so given up his hopelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend tells that the spider's persistence lifted the king out of utter hopelessness.

clue.text: One who begins a race but doesn't finish it

definitions.text: One who begins a race but doesn't finish it

parts.words: One who begins a race but doesn't finish it
parts.note: the official firing the gun sets the runners off but never runs to the line

explanation.surface: A runner sets off in a race but drops out before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a competitor who drops out; the clue means the official with the pistol, who begins the race and has no finish of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who signals the off is literally the one who begins every race.

clue.text: Looking for scraps?

parts.note: scraps here are fights, so someone looking for them is spoiling for a fight

explanation.surface: A dog noses around for leftover food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' suggests leftovers; it is the informal word for fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eager for fights is aggressive and warlike in temperament.

clue.text: Dispatches produce merriment on board

indicators.note: on board puts the merriment inside the ship's letters

parts.note: in crosswords, on board means within SS, the abbreviation for steamship
merriment shows itself in laughter

explanation.surface: Messages sent out cause amusement aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatches' looks like messages; it is the verb, kills.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them, and slaughters is a synonym for kills.

clue.text: Whip-round for an old Roman

parts.note: a cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip
O is a round shape

explanation.surface: A collection is taken for an ancient Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip-round is an informal collection of money; split apart, it gives a whip and a round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of famous Roman statesmen, the Elder and the Younger.

clue.text: Name of Roman source for investors looking for a return

definitions.text: Name of Roman source for investors looking for a return

parts.words: Name of Roman source for investors looking for a return
parts.note: tourists toss coins into Rome's great fountain so as to return to the city one day

explanation.surface: A Roman financier is named for people seeking a profit on their money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investors looking for a return' suggests profit; the investment is a coin tossed into a fountain, and the return is a trip back to Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome's famous baroque fountain is a water source where visitors throw coins.

clue.text: Why one doesn't give the sack to bad cleaner?

definitions.text: Why one doesn't give the sack

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: An employer explains why a poor cleaner keeps the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' sits between the two pieces and works only on 'cleaner'; 'to' stays as it is at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience with faults or putting up with poor work is why someone is not fired.

clue.text: Hen possibly spotted beetle

definitions.meaning: a hen is a female bird, read as a phrase
a small red beetle with black spots

explanation.definitionFit: The red, black-spotted beetle's name also reads as a female bird, which a hen is.

clue.text: Respect some hesitation in one's excuses, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the hesitation sound inside the word for excuses

parts.note: a defence is the case one makes to excuse oneself
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone shows respect by hesitating while making excuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Deference is courteous regard or respect shown to another.

clue.text: Being so, one may react rashly with unusually ill-grace

definitions.text: Being so, one may react rashly

indicators.note: unusually says the letters are set out in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A person reacts hastily and with unusual bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rashly' seems to mean hastily; it means with a rash, an allergic skin reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergic person may come out in a rash on contact with an irritant.

clue.text: Saving firm beset by money trouble

indicators.note: beset by says the firm is surrounded by the jumbled money
trouble stirs up the letters of the word money

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business beset by money troubles is trying to save.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns MONEY into E...NOMY, which surrounds CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy means thrift, the careful saving of money.

clue.text: I fall awkwardly and thrash around

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters land clumsily in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles clumsily and writhes about.
explanation.definitionFit: To flail is to wave the limbs wildly, thrashing about.

clue.text: Separated and sure to play around

indicators.note: to play around is to mess about, so the letters are messed into a new order

explanation.surface: A separated couple, sure to be unfaithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link word, but its letters join those of 'sure' as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart or into pieces is the sense here, the same as separated.

clue.text: Famous ship built by king in the past

indicators.note: in places the king's letter inside the word for the past

parts.note: ago means in the past
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A celebrated vessel was constructed for a monarch long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason's legendary vessel, sailed in search of the Golden Fleece, is a famous ship.

clue.text: Triad thugs running wild

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are sent off in a new order

explanation.surface: Gangsters from a Chinese crime syndicate are rampaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running wild' reads as one phrase; 'running' is the anagram signal and 'wild' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild here means frantic with worry or grief, which is what distraught means.

clue.text: Plunge right in, displaying energy

indicators.note: in places the right abbreviation inside the word for plunge

parts.note: to plunge into water is to dive

explanation.surface: Someone dives straight in with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plunge right in' reads as one instruction; 'right' gives R, which goes in DIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive means determination and vigour, as in a person of great energy.

clue.text: They entertain vast crowds

definitions.meaning: people who receive and entertain guests

explanation.definitionFit: The plural word covers both people who receive guests and great multitudes.

clue.text: A notion to be cast as the Merchant of Venice

indicators.note: to be cast is to be moulded afresh, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An actor has an idea of being cast in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests theatre casting; it is the anagram signal. In Shakespeare's play the title merchant is Antonio, not Shylock.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's title merchant is this character, who borrows from Shylock.

clue.text: Design on a side plate

indicators.note: to design is to arrange, so the letters are set out in a new pattern

explanation.surface: A pattern decorates the edge of a dinner plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' looks like crockery; it is the verb, to coat a metal by electrolysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodising coats a metal with a protective oxide layer, a kind of plating.

clue.text: French president's palace — see more than once

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and its diocese, a bishop's see
the word see taken as written

explanation.surface: Visitors are urged to go repeatedly to the French president's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' tells you the word see is used twice: once as ELY, an English bishop's see, and once as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Élysée Palace in Paris is the official residence of the French president.

clue.text: Society girl's rejecting a title? Rubbish!

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering high society

indicators.note: rejecting suggests turning something back, so the title is read in reverse

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A debutante spurns a peerage, and someone dismisses it as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or waste fragments.
